CLINICAL STUDY PROTOCOL SYNOPSIS

Protocol Title: A Phase II, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Study to
Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of GSK-9921 in Adult Patients with Moderate-to-Severe
Plaque Psoriasis

Protocol Number: GSK-9921-203
Sponsor: GSK Pharmaceuticals
Version: 1.0
Date: 15-Nov-2026

1. BACKGROUND AND RATIONALE
Plaque psoriasis is a chronic immune-mediated skin disease affecting approximately
2-3% of the global population. GSK-9921 is a novel selective IL-23 inhibitor. Preclinical
studies have shown good tolerability in animal models, and Phase I data demonstrated
an acceptable safety profile in healthy volunteers.

2. OBJECTIVES
Primary Objective:
- To evaluate the efficacy of GSK-9921 compared to placebo in achieving PASI-75
  response at Week 16.

Secondary Objectives:
- To evaluate the safety and tolerability of GSK-9921.
- To assess the proportion of patients achieving PASI-90 and PASI-100.
- To evaluate patient-reported quality of life outcomes (DLQI).

3. STUDY DESIGN
This is a multi-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group
study. Approximately 240 patients will be randomized in a 2:1 ratio to receive either
GSK-9921 300 mg or matching placebo, administered subcutaneously every 4 weeks for
16 weeks.

4. STUDY POPULATION
Inclusion Criteria:
- Adults aged 18-75 years.
- Diagnosis of moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis for at least 6 months.
- PASI score >= 12 and body surface area (BSA) involvement >= 10% at screening.

Exclusion Criteria:
- History of active tuberculosis or other serious infections within 6 months.
- Prior exposure to any IL-23 or IL-17 inhibitor.
- Pregnant or breastfeeding women.

5. TREATMENT AND DOSING
GSK-9921 300 mg or placebo will be administered via subcutaneous injection at Weeks
0, 4, 8, 12, and 16. Dose adjustments are not permitted during the treatment period.

6. EFFICACY ASSESSMENTS
PASI score, BSA, and Investigator Global Assessment (IGA) will be assessed at
Screening, Baseline, and Weeks 4, 8, 12, and 16.

7. SAFETY ASSESSMENTS
Adverse events (AEs) and serious adverse events (SAEs) will be collected throughout
the study. Routine laboratory tests (hematology, chemistry, urinalysis) will be
performed at each visit. Patients will be monitored for signs of infection given the
immunomodulatory mechanism of action.

8. STATISTICAL CONSIDERATIONS
A sample size of 240 patients (160 active, 80 placebo) provides approximately 90%
power to detect a 30% difference in PASI-75 response rate between groups, assuming a
two-sided alpha of 0.05.

9. REFERENCES
1. International Council for Harmonisation (ICH) E6(R2) Good Clinical Practice.
2. FDA Guidance for Industry: Psoriasis - Developing Drugs for Treatment, 2018.

--- END OF SYNOPSIS ---
reference_notes:
COMPLETENESS: Missing Scope section, missing Risk Assessment section, missing Approval/Sign-off section. Methodology present but lacks randomization/blinding detail. Safety Data present but lacks a detailed monitoring plan/stopping criteria.
COMPLIANCE: Unsupported efficacy/safety claims ('good tolerability', 'acceptable safety profile') without supporting data/citations (ICH E6(R2)); missing disclosure of infection risk tied to the immunomodulatory mechanism; exclusion criteria omit history of malignancy/autoimmune disease; no mandatory pregnancy testing specified; no statistical method for handling missing data.
CLARITY: Undefined acronyms on first use (PASI, DLQI, IGA, BSA); inconsistent terminology for efficacy endpoints; dense technical jargon without explanation (e.g., two-sided alpha of 0.05); 'serious infections' not defined.
SAFETY: No detail on adverse-event management/dose adjustment or discontinuation criteria; no mention of Phase I observed AEs; monitoring limited to routine labs and infection signs only.
EXPECTED VERDICT: Approve with changes.

CLINICAL STUDY PROTOCOL SYNOPSIS

Protocol Title: A Phase III, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Study to
Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of GSK-4410 in Adult Patients with Type 2 Diabetes
Mellitus

Protocol Number: GSK-4410-301
Sponsor: GSK Pharmaceuticals
Version: 2.1
Date: 01-Oct-2026

1. TITLE AND HEADER
See above. This protocol synopsis is intended for IND submission to FDA and CTA
submission to EMA.

2. SCOPE
This protocol defines the design, conduct, and analysis of a confirmatory Phase III
trial of GSK-4410, a once-daily oral GLP-1/GIP dual agonist, in adults with inadequately
controlled Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM). The scope is limited to adult outpatients
across 85 sites in North America, Europe, and Asia-Pacific; pediatric and
hospitalized populations are explicitly out of scope and will be addressed in
separate protocols.

3. OBJECTIVES
Primary Objective:
- To evaluate the change from baseline in glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c, a measure of
  average blood glucose over approximately 3 months) at Week 52 for GSK-4410 versus
  placebo.

Secondary Objectives:
- To evaluate the proportion of patients achieving HbA1c < 7.0%.
- To evaluate change from baseline in body weight.
- To characterize the pharmacokinetic (PK) profile of GSK-4410.

4. METHODOLOGY
This is a multi-center, randomized (1:1:1), double-blind, placebo- and
active-controlled, parallel-group study comparing GSK-4410 10 mg, GSK-4410 20 mg,
and placebo, with open-label metformin background therapy. Randomization will be
stratified by baseline HbA1c (<8.5% vs >=8.5%) and use an interactive web response
system (IWRS) with permuted-block randomization (block size of 6). Blinding will be
maintained via matched placebo tablets and a double-dummy design; an independent
unblinded statistician will perform interim analyses. Approximately 1,200 patients
will be enrolled to provide 90% power to detect a 0.5% between-group difference in
HbA1c, assuming a two-sided alpha of 0.05 and 15% dropout.

5. STUDY POPULATION
Inclusion Criteria:
- Adults aged 18-75 years with T2DM diagnosed >= 6 months prior to screening.
- HbA1c between 7.5% and 10.5% at screening, inclusive.
- Body mass index (BMI) between 25 and 45 kg/m^2.
- Stable metformin dose for >= 8 weeks prior to screening.

Exclusion Criteria:
- History of type 1 diabetes mellitus or diabetic ketoacidosis.
- History of pancreatitis, medullary thyroid carcinoma, or Multiple Endocrine
  Neoplasia syndrome type 2 (MEN2).
- Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) < 30 mL/min/1.73m^2.
- Pregnant or breastfeeding women; women of childbearing potential must have a
  negative serum pregnancy test at screening and use protocol-specified
  contraception throughout the study.
- History of malignancy within the past 5 years, except treated basal cell
  carcinoma.

6. TREATMENT AND DOSING
GSK-4410 (10 mg or 20 mg) or matching placebo will be administered orally once
daily, in the morning, with or without food, for 52 weeks. Dose titration from 10 mg
to 20 mg will occur at Week 4 per a pre-specified titration schedule to improve
gastrointestinal tolerability; down-titration is permitted for tolerability per
Section 6.2.

7. EFFICACY ASSESSMENTS
HbA1c, fasting plasma glucose, and body weight will be measured at Screening,
Baseline, and Weeks 4, 12, 24, 36, and 52. Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) will
be performed in a subset of 200 patients.

8. SAFETY ASSESSMENTS
Adverse events (AEs) and serious adverse events (SAEs) will be collected from
informed consent through 30 days after last dose. Specific solicited AEs for this
drug class (nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, pancreatitis signs/symptoms) will be
actively queried at each visit. Calcitonin levels will be monitored given the
mechanism-related theoretical risk of C-cell hyperplasia observed in rodent
studies (not confirmed in non-human primates or human data to date). A Data Safety
Monitoring Board (DSMB) will review unblinded safety data every 6 months and has
authority to recommend study modification or termination. Stopping rules are
pre-specified in Section 8.4 (e.g., confirmed pancreatitis, calcitonin >
2x ULN confirmed on repeat testing).

9. RISK ASSESSMENT
The principal risks of GSK-4410 are gastrointestinal (nausea, vomiting, diarrhea),
hypoglycemia when combined with insulin secretagogues, and a theoretical risk of
thyroid C-cell tumors based on rodent carcinogenicity data (clinical relevance to
humans not established). Mitigation measures include dose titration, exclusion of
patients with relevant thyroid/pancreatic history, solicited AE queries, and DSMB
oversight. Overall benefit-risk is considered favorable for the target population
based on totality of Phase II data (Protocol GSK-4410-204) showing a 1.8%
placebo-adjusted HbA1c reduction with a manageable GI tolerability profile.

10. STATISTICAL CONSIDERATIONS
The primary analysis will use a mixed model for repeated measures (MMRM) on the
full analysis set (FAS), with multiple imputation as a sensitivity analysis for
missing data. A hierarchical testing procedure will control the family-wise Type I
error rate across the two dose levels and secondary endpoints.

11. REFERENCES
1. International Council for Harmonisation (ICH) E6(R2) Good Clinical Practice.
2. ICH E9 Statistical Principles for Clinical Trials.
3. FDA Guidance for Industry: Diabetes Mellitus - Developing Drugs and Therapeutic
   Biologics for Treatment and Prevention, 2020.
4. GSK-4410-204 Phase II Clinical Study Report, 2025 (data on file).

12. APPROVAL / SIGN-OFF
This protocol has been reviewed and approved by the Sponsor's Clinical Development
Lead, Global Safety Officer, and Biostatistics Lead. Institutional Review
Board/Independent Ethics Committee (IRB/IEC) approval is required at each site
prior to enrollment. Signatures on file with the Sponsor's Clinical Trial Master
File (TMF).

--- END OF SYNOPSIS ---
reference_notes:
This is a well-formed protocol synopsis intended as a 'near-complete' positive control. COMPLETENESS: All required sections are present (Title, Scope, Objectives, Methodology, Risk Assessment, Safety Data, References, Approval/Sign-off) with reasonable detail including randomization/blinding methodology and a DSMB.
COMPLIANCE: Efficacy/safety claims are supported by a cited Phase II study (GSK-4410-204); known class risks (thyroid C-cell tumors, pancreatitis) are disclosed with appropriate caveats about human relevance; pregnancy testing and contraception requirements are specified; missing-data handling (MMRM, multiple imputation) and multiplicity control are specified. Reviewers may still flag minor items such as lack of explicit dose-adjustment detail for hepatic impairment, but overall this document should score materially better on compliance/completeness than a document with major gaps.
CLARITY: Acronyms are generally defined at first use (HbA1c, IWRS, DSMB); a few secondary acronyms (CGM, MMRM) are used without expansion and could be flagged as minor.
SAFETY: Risk assessment explicitly discusses mechanism-based theoretical risks with mitigation, monitoring (calcitonin, solicited GI AEs), stopping rules, and DSMB oversight.
EXPECTED VERDICT: Approve (or Approve with minor changes).

INVESTIGATOR'S BROCHURE SUMMARY (EXCERPT)

Product: GSK-7734 (oral small-molecule JAK1 inhibitor)
Indication: Moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis
Version: 4.0
Date: 03-Mar-2026

BACKGROUND
GSK-7734 works really well and is basically safe for most patients. Our drug is
better than competitor products on the market and has essentially no serious
risks when used as directed. Patients love it.

NONCLINICAL OVERVIEW
Animal studies were conducted. Everything looked fine. No further details are
provided in this excerpt.

CLINICAL EXPERIENCE TO DATE
Phase I and Phase II studies have been completed. The drug was well tolerated.
Efficacy was demonstrated. Full data tables are available upon request but are
not included here.

KNOWN AND POTENTIAL RISKS
JAK inhibitors as a class have been associated with increased risk of serious
infections (including herpes zoster), major adverse cardiovascular events
(MACE), venous thromboembolism (VTE), malignancy, and thrombosis, per FDA boxed
warning requirements for this drug class (see FDA Drug Safety Communication,
2021). This excerpt does not quantify the observed incidence of these events in
GSK-7734 trials, nor does it describe monitoring requirements (e.g., lipid
panels, lymphocyte counts) or dose-adjustment criteria for hepatic/renal
impairment.

GUIDANCE FOR INVESTIGATORS
Investigators should use clinical judgement. Refer questions to the medical
monitor.

REFERENCES
None listed in this excerpt.

--- END OF EXCERPT ---
reference_notes:
This document is deliberately poor and should receive a strongly negative review. COMPLIANCE: Promotional, unsupported marketing-style claims ('works really well', 'basically safe', 'better than competitor products', 'Patients love it') are inappropriate for an Investigator's Brochure and violate ICH E6(R2) standards for objective, data-driven safety communication. The known JAK-inhibitor class boxed-warning risks (serious infection, MACE, VTE, malignancy, thrombosis) are named but not quantified with trial incidence data, and no monitoring or dose-adjustment guidance is given despite being standard-of-care for this drug class.
COMPLETENESS: Nonclinical Overview and Clinical Experience sections are placeholders with no actual data ('Everything looked fine', 'data tables available upon request'); no References section; no sign-off/approval section.
CLARITY: Vague, non-specific statements throughout ('Investigators should use clinical judgement') provide no actionable guidance.
SAFETY: Does not quantify observed AE incidence, does not describe required monitoring (lipid panel, lymphocyte counts) or hepatic/renal dose adjustments for a boxed-warning drug class.
EXPECTED VERDICT: Reject (requires substantial rewrite before resubmission).

PACKAGE INSERT / PRESCRIBING INFORMATION (DRAFT EXCERPT)

Product Name: Cardiozine (fictional brand) / GSK-5512 (generic substance)
Dosage Form: Oral tablet, 50 mg and 100 mg
Indication: Adjunct therapy for chronic heart failure with reduced ejection
fraction (HFrEF) in adults

1. INDICATIONS AND USAGE
Cardiozine is indicated for the tx of HFrEF pts, NYHA class II-III, to reduce
the risk of CV death and HF hospitalization.

2. DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION
Start at 50mg once a day. May increase to 100mg based on response. Take with or
without food. Renal adjustment: see dosing table (not included in this
excerpt).

3. CONTRAINDICATIONS
- Known hypersensitivity to Cardiozine or its excipients.
- Concurrent use with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors (interaction not further
  described in this excerpt).

4. WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS
- Hyperkalemia: monitor serum potassium.
- Hypotension: use caution in volume-depleted pts.
- Renal function: monitor eGFR periodically; the periodicity and specific
  action thresholds are not specified in this excerpt.

5. ADVERSE REACTIONS
The most commonly reported adverse reactions (incidence >= 5%) in clinical
trials were dizziness, hyperkalemia, and hypotension. Specific incidence rates
versus comparator are not provided in this excerpt.

6. DRUG INTERACTIONS
May interact with other drugs. Consult full prescribing information (not
included) for a complete list.

7. USE IN SPECIFIC POPULATIONS
Pregnancy: Limited data. Lactation: Not recommended. Pediatric use: Safety and
efficacy not established. Geriatric use: No overall differences in safety or
efficacy observed relative to younger patients; this statement is not
supported by referenced subgroup data in this excerpt.

8. CLINICAL STUDIES
Cardiozine was studied in a pivotal Phase III trial (CARDIOZINE-HF-301, n =
4,200) that demonstrated a statistically significant reduction in the composite
endpoint of CV death or HF hospitalization versus placebo (HR not stated in
this excerpt; full results pending publication).

--- END OF DRAFT EXCERPT ---
reference_notes:
COMPLETENESS: Core prescribing-information sections are present (Indications, Dosage, Contraindications, Warnings, Adverse Reactions, Drug Interactions, Use in Specific Populations, Clinical Studies) but several are explicitly incomplete ('not included in this excerpt', 'not further described'), notably the renal dosing table and full drug-interaction list.
CLARITY: Uses non-standard abbreviations/shorthand ('tx', 'pts', 'CV', '50mg') inappropriate for formal prescribing information; inconsistent spacing/formatting of dose units.
COMPLIANCE: Adverse reaction incidence is stated only as ">= 5%" without comparator rates or a table, which is insufficient for FDA/EMA labeling standards; geriatric-use statement claims no safety/efficacy differences without citing supporting subgroup data; the pivotal trial result is referenced without the actual hazard ratio or p-value.
SAFETY: Hyperkalemia/hypotension/renal monitoring are mentioned but lack specific thresholds, periodicity, or stopping/action criteria; CYP3A4 interaction is flagged as a contraindication without explaining the mechanism or risk.
EXPECTED VERDICT: Approve with changes (major revisions needed before the excerpt could be finalized).

PERIODIC SAFETY UPDATE REPORT (PSUR) - EXECUTIVE SUMMARY (EXCERPT)

Product: GSK-2290 (monoclonal antibody, anti-IL-5)
Indication: Severe eosinophilic asthma
Reporting Period: 01-Jan-2025 to 31-Dec-2025
Version: 1.0
Date: 20-Feb-2026

1. INTRODUCTION
This PSUR covers the reporting period above for GSK-2290, marketed in 42
countries. Worldwide exposure is estimated at approximately 85,000
patient-years based on sales data.

2. WORLDWIDE MARKETING AUTHORIZATION STATUS
GSK-2290 is approved in the US, EU, Japan, and 39 other countries for severe
eosinophilic asthma as an add-on maintenance treatment.

3. ACTIONS TAKEN FOR SAFETY REASONS
No regulatory actions, label changes, or risk minimization measures were
implemented during this reporting period.

4. CHANGES TO REFERENCE SAFETY INFORMATION
No changes to the Company Core Data Sheet (CCDS) during this period.

5. ESTIMATED EXPOSURE
Approximately 85,000 patient-years of post-marketing exposure, plus 3,200
patients across ongoing and completed clinical trials.

6. PRESENTATION OF INDIVIDUAL CASE SAFETY REPORTS
A total of 410 serious adverse event (SAE) cases were received during the
period, including 18 cases of serious hypersensitivity reactions and 6 fatal
cases assessed as unrelated to study drug by the investigator. Hypersensitivity
reactions, including anaphylaxis, are an identified risk per the Risk
Management Plan (RMP) and are listed in the current product label. No new
unexpected serious adverse reactions were identified in this period.

7. SIGNALS AND EVALUATION
One potential new safety signal (increased incidence of injection-site nodules)
was evaluated and determined not to require label changes based on available
data; continued monitoring was recommended.

8. BENEFIT-RISK ANALYSIS
Based on cumulative safety and efficacy data, the benefit-risk balance for
GSK-2290 in the approved indication remains favorable. No changes to the
benefit-risk conclusion are proposed in this period.

9. CONCLUSION
No new safety concerns were identified that would warrant a change to the
current risk management plan. Routine pharmacovigilance activities will
continue per the RMP.

REFERENCES
1. ICH E2C(R2) Periodic Benefit-Risk Evaluation Report.
2. GSK-2290 Risk Management Plan, v6.0, 2025.

APPROVAL
Reviewed and approved by Global Patient Safety and Regulatory Affairs.

--- END OF EXCERPT ---
reference_notes:
This is a well-structured, compliant Periodic Safety Update Report executive summary and should score favorably. COMPLETENESS: Standard ICH E2C(R2) PSUR sections are all present: introduction, marketing authorization status, actions taken, RSI changes, exposure estimates, case presentation, signal evaluation, benefit-risk analysis, conclusion, references, and approval/sign-off.
COMPLIANCE: Identified risks (hypersensitivity) are correctly cross-referenced to the Risk Management Plan; signal evaluation process is described; benefit-risk conclusion is stated with rationale; cites ICH E2C(R2) appropriately.
CLARITY: Terminology is consistent and standard for pharmacovigilance documents (SAE, CCDS, RMP all used correctly); minor opportunity to spell out acronyms like CCDS on first use for a general audience.
SAFETY: Reports concrete counts (410 SAEs, 18 hypersensitivity cases, 6 fatal cases with causality assessment) and an evaluated new signal (injection-site nodules) with a documented monitoring decision, which is appropriately detailed safety reporting.
EXPECTED VERDICT: Approve.
